Updated the tool registry, translations, page introduction/guide/FAQs, attachment rules, Split/Extract title and copy, and related regression tests. `npm.cmd test` passes 141/141; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with the existing `docx` buffer-externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Browser smoke tests completed both directions: a synthetic DOCX produced an 18,169-byte PDF Blob that PDF.js reopened as one A4 page with one image and no searchable text; rendering that page at 596×842 px confirmed nonblank content. A synthetic text PDF produced a 7.3 KB DOCX result. At 320 and 390 px, the Word → PDF workspace had no horizontal overflow (305 px and 375 px document widths). The earlier DOCX-content inspection remains evidence for PDF → Word. Browser download-to-disk, varied/complex DOCX layouts, OCR conversion, and cross-browser/accessibility behavior remain unverified. Next: verify download-to-disk and representative complex DOCX layouts. No commit was made.

**Unified Split PDF modes and percentage-based sections (2026-11-01):** Consolidated selected-page extraction, per-page splitting, and balanced percentage-based splitting into `/split`; `/extract-pages` redirects there. The percentage slider creates 2–10 consecutive page groups, keeps previews paginated, and labels each page's group without allocating labels for every page. PDF output generation now uses a tested helper. The full suite passes 134/134; focused Split PDF tests pass 35/35; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with the existing `docx` buffer-externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Browser verification with a 10-page fixture rendered all 10 previews, showed 40%/30%/30% groups for three parts, generated three part PDFs, generated selected-page extraction for pages 2 and 8, and produced a ZIP card for splitting every page. Automated output tests reloaded the generated part PDFs and verified their page counts/order by distinct page dimensions. Browser download-to-disk and the extracted output's page contents remain unverified. Updated the tool registry, route, shared page grid, tool-page content, `IDEA.md`, and Split evidence. No commit was made; preserve the other uncommitted changes.

**Packaging large Split PDF outputs (2026-11-01):** Split All Pages now packages more than three single-page PDFs into one client-side ZIP download; three or fewer remain individual PDF downloads. Reused the ZIP writer for PDF files, expanded its entry limit to the ZIP32 maximum, and retained an explicit fallback to individual downloads if archive creation fails. Updated the Split instructions/FAQ and attachment guidance. Regression tests failed before implementation; focused archive/responsive tests pass 11/11 and the full suite passes 126/126. Tests inspect ZIP entries and reload the contained PDFs to verify their one-page counts and dimensions; a 51-entry archive also passes. The production build succeeds with the existing `docx` buffer-externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Browser processing showed one ZIP card for a four-page fixture and three PDF cards for a three-page fixture. The browser did not expose a download event, so save-to-disk behavior remains unverified. ZIP32 size limits remain; if archive creation fails, the individual PDFs are offered with an error message. No commit was made.

**Recovering Split PDF page-tree roots (2026-11-01):** Fixed the Split flow for PDFs whose catalog `/Pages` root has `/Kids` and `/Count` but omits `/Type /Pages`. Split now restores the missing root type only after validating the tree shape and child nodes. The same local file then reports 911 pages without extracting content or generating a copy. A synthetic one-page regression verifies recovery, copy, save, and reload. `npm.cmd test` passes 99/99; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Actual page extraction/download from the supplied book was not performed.

## Unlock PDF implementation — 2026-10-29
- Added the user-approved exact runtime dependency `@pdfsmaller/pdf-decrypt@1.0.1` (MIT, `pdf-lib` peer dependency) and synchronized `package-lock.json`; no unrelated package versions changed. Reviewed its published browser entry point and confirmed the implementation uses Web Crypto and PDF object parsing without a document-upload/network call. The package supports AES-256 R6 and RC4 R2/R3; AES-128 R4 is explicitly unsupported.
- Implemented `/unlock` with a separate component and registry entry under Protect & Repair. It accepts only detected encrypted PDFs, requires a user-supplied password, clears the password from UI state after each attempt, and has explicit wrong-password/unsupported/unencrypted/invalid-file messages. It does not modify the shared validator or other tools' encrypted-input rejection.
- The component decrypts in-browser, independently opens the source with PDF.js using the supplied password to count pages, then loads the output with `pdf-lib` without a password and verifies the output is unencrypted and retains the source page count. It provides a separate manual download and warns users to review signatures, forms, annotations, attachments, and specialized features because the PDF is rewritten.
- Node synthetic-fixture verification used `pdf-lib`, the installed companion encrypt package, and PDF.js: AES-256 R6 and RC4 R3 were identified; correct-password outputs reopened without a password, had two pages, and matched source extracted text; wrong passwords and unencrypted inputs were rejected.
- Browser verification on `/unlock` confirmed the route title/content; AES-256 and RC4 correct-password operations displayed verified two-page outputs; an incorrect password produced an alert and cleared the password field; unencrypted and invalid PDFs were rejected without entering selected-file state. The Protect & Repair category listed all three tools, search surfaced Unlock PDF and opened `/unlock`, and neutral info/status surfaces computed correctly in both light and dark themes. Browser download-event capture was attempted but not observed, so the final download action remains unverified.
- `npm.cmd run build`, `npm.cmd ls --depth=0`, package JSON parsing, targeted VS Code Problems checks, and `git diff --check` passed. The build emitted existing `docx`/`buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; the app JS chunk is 1,818.80 kB minified. A controlled before/after build was not run, so package-only bundle impact is unmeasured.
- Next: verify a real browser download and, if available, test an independently sourced AES-128 R4 fixture to confirm the documented unsupported-encryption message. Review output fidelity for PDFs with forms, annotations, attachments, and signatures.

## Watermark PDF — 2026-10-28
- Added `src/components/PdfWatermarker.jsx`, registered `/watermark` in `src/App.jsx`, and added an active matching homepage card in `src/components/Home.jsx`.
- Uses installed `pdf-lib` APIs (`drawText`, `StandardFonts.Helvetica`, `rgb`, `degrees`, and text opacity) to add centered, rotated text without rasterizing pages or changing the source file.
- Supports text, 8–96 pt size, colour, -180° to 180° rotation, 0–100% opacity, all pages, and strict 1-based page/range selection.
- Also supports independent page numbering with starting number, top/bottom placement, alignment, colour, size, margin, and an independent page range.
- Displays file size and loaded page count; supports replacing, removing, and resetting the selected file. Output page count and order are retained.
- Limitations: built-in Helvetica has WinAnsi character coverage, so unsupported text is rejected; password-protected PDFs are not supported.

## Organize, Redact, Sign, and category navigation
- Added `src/components/OrganizePdf.jsx`, `src/components/RedactPdf.jsx`, and `src/components/SignPdf.jsx`, registered their routes in `src/App.jsx`, and added their active cards to the existing category-grouped homepage.
- Organize PDF reorders, rotates, and removes pages with real previews, then uses `pdf-lib` to preserve the selected pages and produce a new document. The tested output retained two pages in reordered source order, retained text, and applied the configured 90-degree rotation.
- Redact PDF draws opaque masks and outputs rasterized pages so masked source content is not left extractable beneath a cover. Browser verification confirmed the same page count, no extracted text on the output pages, an opaque black sample mask pixel, and visible unmasked source content. Rasterization loses selectable text, vector fidelity, links, forms, and other interactive features.
- Sign PDF supports typed, drawn, and PNG/JPEG signature marks, page selection, and placement controls. Outputs are visible marks only; they do not authenticate identity, prevent document changes, or constitute certificate-backed signatures.
- Category-aware related tools render as a responsive same-category grid (excluding the current tool). Browser checks confirmed Sign shows only Watermark and Redact; Organize shows three peers under “Other organizing tools”.
- Menu dismissal, focus restoration, mobile category switching, search keyboard behavior, and homepage card focus/activation were verified; detailed evidence is in the current navigation section and checklist.
- Upload controls were checked in light and dark themes for normal, hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and simulated drag-active states. Dark menu panel and text colors were also checked; computed styles and browser evidence are recorded in the checklist.
- Unlock PDF is now implemented and registered using the approved browser-side decryption dependency. See the 2026-10-29 implementation section above for supported encryption, verification evidence, and remaining download/fidelity checks.
